newsitem.title: PERU: Bullish Atacocha soars on Lima bolsa.
newsitem.headline: Bullish Atacocha soars on Lima bolsa.

text.p: Polymetallic miner Atacocha leapt 7.69 percent by mid-session Wednesday on the Lima Stock Exchange, buoyed by zinc prices and the Peruvian mining sector's bull run, brokers said.
Atacocha's share price rose to 2.10 soles in volume of 1.17 million shares by 11:40 a.m. local (1640 GMT), according to the exchange.
"The reason is the rise in the international price of zinc," said Julio Alcalde, of MGS y Asociados brokerage.

Atacocha and another miner, Morococha, which also soared by mid-session 10.08 percent to 6.6 soles on 1.24 million shares, have been leading a surge in the mining sector this month. Miners' liquid labor shares have gained more than 140 percent so far this year, compared to the bolsa's overalll rise of about 40 percent.
This month, investors typically have been jumping from one mining stock to another during each session as the individual company's price reaches its perceived ceiling for the day.
Players usually start buying Atacocha or Morococha before moving on to second-tier polymetallic miners such as Milpo and Perubar.

Solid individual company performances have attracted investors to the mining sector where zinc producers have seen the largest gains due to elevated metal prices on interational markets, brokers said.
